attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own newsletter post, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the hedge 'appears to be' and the exclusivity scope. It is correctly an observation about the post date. Because the hedge is epistemic, this is not a firm claim of exclusivity.

contract.note: The contract correctly finds no binary test. 'Appears' hedges the claim, and 'available' could mean approved, contracted, or operationally accessible. Choosing one of those would add a commitment the speaker did not make.

evidence.note: Reuters, 12 Feb 2026, reports Anthropic as the only company available in classified settings through third parties. This explains why it looked that way, but it predates the post and cannot test a hedged exclusivity claim.
OpenAI's own disclosure, 27-28 Feb 2026, announces an agreement for classified deployment. It bears on an approval-based reading of 'available' but does not show operational availability on March 3.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged observation: Claude 'appears to be' the only model available for classified military operations. The speaker gave no meaning for 'available' and no evidentiary threshold. Reuters (e1) explains the appearance, and OpenAI's announced agreement (e2) complicates one reading. Neither can settle a hedged claim without adding a definition the speaker never supplied, so it cannot be scored.
